Create a Word reference document from a brand.yml file

Source: R/brand_reference_docx.R
brand_reference_docx.Rd

brand_reference_docx() creates a Word document for use as a Quarto or Pandoc reference document (the reference-doc option for docx output) using the colors and typography from a brand.yml file.

By default, the function starts from Pandoc's default reference.docx (so every style Pandoc uses exists) and merges the brand settings into the existing style definitions. Styles are edited with xml2, rather than with officer::docx_set_paragraph_style(), because that function replaces a style wholesale and drops properties the brand doesn't set (e.g. the heading outline levels Word uses for the table of contents).

pandoc_reference_docx() writes Pandoc's default reference.docx to a file using Quarto's bundled Pandoc (if Quarto is installed) or Pandoc.

Usage

brand_reference_docx(
  brand = NULL,
  path = NULL,
  reference = NULL,
  overwrite = TRUE,
  quiet = FALSE
)

pandoc_reference_docx(path = tempfile(fileext = ".docx"))

Arguments

brand

Path to a brand.yml file or a directory containing one, a brand_yml object from brand.yml::read_brand_yml(), or a list with the brand settings (e.g. from yaml12::read_yaml()). If NULL (default), the path is taken from the BRAND_YML_PATH environment variable or, if that is not set, found by searching the working directory and its parent directories for _brand.yml or _brand.yaml, either directly or in a brand or _brand subdirectory (the same search used by Quarto and brand.yml::read_brand_yml()).

path

Optional file path for the output docx file. If NULL (default), the document is not written to a file.

reference

Optional path to a docx file or a rdocx object to use as the starting reference document. If NULL (default), Pandoc's default reference.docx is used (which requires Quarto or Pandoc). Styles named in defaults.docx.styles must exist in the reference document. Note that a rdocx object is modified in place (as with other officer functions).

overwrite

If TRUE (default), remove file at path if it already exists. If FALSE and file exists, this function aborts.

quiet

If TRUE, suppress the message reporting the path of the written file. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

brand_reference_docx() returns a rdocx object (invisibly if path is supplied). pandoc_reference_docx() returns path.

Brand settings

The following brand.yml settings are used:

  • color: palette and color roles (e.g. primary or foreground). Wherever a color is used, it can be a hex value, a CSS color name, an rgb() value, a palette name, or a color role.

  • typography.base: family, size, weight, and line-height for the document defaults and the Normal style.

  • typography.headings: family, weight, style, color, and line-height for the Heading 1-9, TOC Heading, and Title styles.

  • typography.link: color, background-color, weight, and decoration for the Hyperlink style.

  • typography.monospace-inline (inheriting from typography.monospace): family, size, weight, color, and background-color for the Verbatim Char style.

  • typography.monospace-block (inheriting from typography.monospace): background-color (as paragraph shading), line-height, color, family, size, and weight for the Source Code style used for code blocks. Pandoc's default reference document has no Source Code style, so it is created if monospace-block sets background-color, line-height, or color; otherwise, Pandoc creates the style when rendering (with shading from the highlight style).

Pandoc formats the text in code blocks with the Verbatim Char style (or syntax highlighting styles based on it), which takes precedence over the Source Code style. As a result, monospace-block values for family, size, weight, and color only apply if monospace-inline doesn't set a different value, and highlighted code keeps the token colors and shading from the highlight style (set with the Quarto highlight-style option).

brand.yml has no Word-specific options, so additional settings are read from defaults.docx (the brand.yml section for format-specific options):

  • defaults.docx.styles: a list of style settings named by style ID (e.g. Heading1 or BodyText) or style name (e.g. Body Text). Each style supports the typography fields family, size, weight, style, color, background-color, decoration, and line-height plus the paragraph fields space-before, space-after, indent-left, and keep-with-next. The Table style supports border-color, border-width, cell-padding (with top, bottom, left, and right), and header (typography fields for the first row).

  • defaults.docx.page: size ("letter", "legal", or "a4"), margins (with top, bottom, left, right, header, footer, and gutter), and footer (with text, align, size, color, and family). In the footer text, {page} and {pages} are replaced with the page number and page count. Margins that aren't set keep the reference document's value (or Word's default of 1in for the page and 0.5in for the header and footer).

Field names can use hyphens (as in the brand.yml spec) or underscores (as in objects from brand.yml::read_brand_yml()).

Sizes can use pt, in, cm, mm, px, rem, or em units (bare numbers are treated as pt). Following CSS, 1rem and 1em are 16px (12pt). A unitless line-height is a multiple of the font size; a line-height with units sets an exact line height. Font weights can be numbers (100-900) or CSS weight names (e.g. "semi-bold"); a weight of 600 or more is bold.

These brand.yml settings are not used: color.background (Word documents don't have a page color by default), typography.fonts (fonts are not embedded, so the font families must be installed wherever the document is opened), and decoration: overline (Word has no overline).

See system.file("extdata", "_brand.yml", package = "officerExtras") for an example.

Table borders and other details that the brand doesn't cover can be edited by hand in Word afterwards (but re-creating the reference document overwrites those edits).

Page settings and sections

The defaults.docx.page settings (page size, margins, and footer) are stored in the reference document's section properties. Pandoc copies them to the last section of the rendered document, so they don't always apply to every page:

  • Quarto's .landscape divs add section breaks with no footer, no margins, and an A4 landscape page size, so the pages before and in a landscape section lose the footer and page settings.

  • A custom Pandoc OpenXML template (the template option for docx output, e.g. as used by the better-word Quarto extension) replaces the section properties if it doesn't use the $sectpr$ variable.

Use docx_sync_sections() on the rendered document (e.g. in a Quarto post-render script) to copy the footer and page settings from the last section to every other section. The reference document only controls styles and these defaults, not the document structure (e.g. the title block or table of contents), which a custom template controls.

Examples

if (nzchar(Sys.which("quarto")) || nzchar(Sys.which("pandoc"))) {
  brand_path <- system.file("extdata", "_brand.yml", package = "officerExtras")

  withr::with_tempdir({
    brand_reference_docx(brand_path, path = "reference.docx")
  })
}
